 Klay Thompson finished Wednesday’s overtime win over the Clippers with 30 points (11-of-22 FGs), five rebounds, three assists, one block and eight three-pointers.
 Thompson had his best game of the season on Wednesday, shooting 8-of-17 from beyond the arc. His last three-pointer was the most important, as the Heat guard/forward hit one from the left corner with one second remaining in overtime to give Miami the win. Inconsistent in his first five games, Thompson has scored at least 19 points in three straight. Could he be returning to fantasy relevance? The Heat play two more games this week, so it may not be a bad time to stream Klay if you need three-pointers. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Klay Thompson lit up the Lakers with 19 points (7-of-11 FGs), one rebound, one assist and four three-pointers on Monday. 
 Thompson has shrugged off a slow start to the season and is starting to figure things out. Over the last two games, he has averaged 22 points and 5.5 triples per game while shooting at least 60 percent from the floor. Thompson likely won’t stay this hot, but he’ll have his hot streaks throughout the year. He’ll look to keep it going against the Clippers on Wednesday. 
 Klay Thompson 
 MIA 
 Guard-Forward 
 #11 
 Klay Thompson accumulated 25 points (9-of-14 FGs), three assists and seven three-pointers in Friday’s win over the Pacers. 
 Entering Friday, Thompson was shooting 31.7 percent from the field and 32.1 percent from three. To say a night like Friday was needed would be an understatement. Against the Pacers, Thompson shot 7-of-12 from beyond the arc, and 25 points is the most he has scored in a game since January 15, as a member of the Mavericks. With neither Giannis Antetokounmpo nor Bam Adebayo offering much perimeter shooting as Miami’s top two offensive options, Thompson needs to hit shots consistently. Friday’s 145-point outburst showed what can happen when he and the other Heat shooters are productive. 
 Klay Thompson 
 MIA 
 Guard-Forward 
 #11 
 Klay Thompson contributed 14 points (5-of-12 FGs), three rebounds, one steal and four three-pointers against the Hornets on Saturday. 
 Following a rough shooting performance against the Pistons on Friday, Thompson was able to find his shot in this one. He set season highs for points and three-pointers, though it wasn’t enough for them to get their first win of the season. For now, Thompson should continue to start and provide floor spacing. If you’re looking for production outside of triples, it’s best to look elsewhere.

 #11 
 Klay Thompson notched 10 points (3-of-6 FGs, 1-of-1 FTs), one rebound and three three-pointers in Wednesday’s loss to the Timberwolves. 
 After making two of his three three-point attempts and scoring six points in the first quarter, Thompson did not provide much value in his official Heat debut. While starting was a positive for the veteran guard, he played just 16 minutes. Meanwhile, Tim Hardaway Jr. (three points, four rebounds, one assist, one steal and one three-pointer) logged 18 minutes off the bench. Outside of deep leagues where you need three-pointers, you gain little by rostering Thompson.

 Klay Thompson tallied five points (2-of-7 FGs), one rebound, three assists, one steal, three blocks and one three-pointer in Thursday’s exhibition against the Pelicans. 
 Blocked shots have never been a huge part of Thompson’s game, so there’s no need to read into his performance against the Pelicans. However, it was good to see the veteran sharpshooter active on the defensive end of the floor. Thompson hasn’t shot well in Miami’s first two preseason games, but starting gives him a chance to return to fantasy relevance in 2026-27. 
 Tim Hardaway 
 MIA 
 Guard 
 #10 
 Tim Hardaway Jr. tallied 14 points (4-of-4 FGs, 3-of-3 FTs) and three three-pointers in Saturday’s exhibition against the Raptors. 
 With a starting lineup that includes two limited perimeter shooters, Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo, the Heat clearly need players who can provide spacing. They signed Hardaway for that reason, and he had an excellent preseason debut on Saturday. The veteran guard didn’t miss a shot from the field, making all three of his three-point attempts. Klay Thompson (zero points, two rebounds in 13 minutes) was the fifth starter, but it’s unknown if that will hold once the regular season begins. Regardless of what Erik Spoelstra decides, Hardaway could have value for managers in deeper leagues seeking three-point production. 
 Klay Thompson 
 MIA 
 Guard 
 #11 
 Davion Mitchell, Klay Thompson, Andrew Wiggins, Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo started Saturday’s exhibition against the Raptors. 
 Antetokounmpo’s Heat preseason debut is Miami’s biggest storyline, but Thompson’s fifth-man role also merits mention. He came off the bench for most of his two seasons in Dallas, which may have contributed to the veteran sharpshooter’s failure to provide consistent fantasy value. Thompson is one player expected to provide the perimeter shooting that Miami needs to keep the paint somewhat clear for Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo. That would also enhance Thompson’s fantasy outlook, making him a player worth selecting in the latter rounds of standard league drafts. 
 Klay Thompson 
 MIA 
 Guard 
 Hoopshype’s Michael Scotto reports that Klay Thompson gave back $9.8 million in a buyout agreement with the Dallas Mavericks. 
 Thompson’s departure from the Mavericks comes with a price. However, the veteran sharpshooter will now move on to the next chapter of his career, which will reportedly be with the Miami Heat. In joining the Heat, Thompson would likely come off the bench and play an important floor-spacing role for a team that could use all the three-point shooting possible. Thompson averaged 11.7 points and shot 38.3 percent from deep last season with Dallas. 
 Klay Thompson 
 MIA 
 Guard 
 #31 
 ESPN’s Shams Charania reports that Klay Thompson is expected to sign a two-year, $13 million deal with the Heat, with a player option for the second season, after clearing waivers following a buyout with the Mavericks. 
 Shortly after NBA insider Chris Haynes reported that Thompson had reached a buyout agreement with Dallas, Shams dropped the news that Thompson was headed to South Beach. Thompson’s final season in Dallas was forgettable, but he’s still an elite shooter, which is exactly what the Heat need to build this team around Giannis Antetokounmpo. There is a chance that Thompson starts alongside Davion Mitchell, Andrew Wiggins, Giannis and Bam Adebayo, though he should play a significant role regardless. Pelle Larsson may take on a smaller role than anticipated with Thompson in town. 
 Klay Thompson 
 DAL 
 Guard 
 #31 
 Christian Clark of The Athletic reports that the Mavericks have explored the trade market for Klay Thompson. 
 Added via sign-and-trade ahead of the 2024-25 season, Thompson’s first two seasons in Dallas have not gone as planned. While his 38.7 percent mark from three is respectable, that is nearly four percentage points lower than his number with the Warriors. Also, the Mavericks have not been a contender in Thompson’s two seasons, especially after former lead executive Nico Harrison decided to trade Luka Dončić to the Lakers. With 16 players on standard contracts and a new lead executive, Masai Ujiri, calling the shots, it’s unsurprising that the Mavericks would reportedly explore the market for Thompson. In July, it was reported that Miami had interest in Thompson, potentially adding another shooter to play off of Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo.

 Brook Lopez amassed 20 points (8-of-11 FGs, 2-of-5 FTs), eight rebounds, one assist, two blocks and two three-pointers in Wednesday’s loss to the Heat.
 After playing 22 minutes in his first start of the season on Monday, Lopez played 35 in Wednesday’s overtime thriller. Given his production in those two starts and Isaiah Jackson’s inability to avoid silly fouls, Lopez may have the starting center job for the foreseeable future. Jackson, who has committed at least four fouls in six of his eight games, played 13 minutes against the Heat and finished with two points, four rebounds, two assists and one steal.

 Darius Garland recorded 26 points (10-of-14 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), one rebound, seven assists and four three-pointers in Wednesday’s loss to the Heat.
 By now, it’s known that category-league managers rostering Garland will likely have to punt turnovers. He racked up six turnovers against the Heat, but the Clippers’ guard had his best shooting night this season. In addition to making 10 of 14 shots from the field, he recorded seven assists, making for a decent night at the office.

 Rui Hachimura accumulated 21 points (7-of-18 FGs, 6-of-7 FTs), nine rebounds, seven assists, one steal and one three-pointer in Wednesday’s loss to the Heat.
 Hachimura has gotten off to a relatively slow start with the Clippers, shooting 37.3 percent from the field and 68.4 percent from the foul line. Add inconsistent production in assists, steals and blocks, and rostering Hachimura in some 10-team leagues isn’t worth discussing. He had a productive night against the Heat, with the seven assists being more than double his total entering the night (three). For Hachimura to be someone you can roster in shallow leagues after the Clippers get guys like Brandon Ingram and Bradley Beal back, nights like Wednesday have to become the norm.

 Giannis Antetokounmpo recorded 27 points (8-of-20 FGs, 11-of-13 FTs), 14 rebounds, six assists, two steals and three blocks in Wednesday’s win over the Clippers.
 On most nights, fantasy managers can expect Giannis to shoot a high percentage from the field but struggle at the foul line. The opposite happened against the Clippers, with the Heat forward shooting 40 percent from the field and 84.6 percent from the foul line. Antetokounmpo finished with a robust stat line that had everything but a three-pointer. The Heat play two more games this week, starting with the Warriors on Thursday.

 Davion Mitchell tallied 11 points (5-of-13 FGs, 1-of-1 FTs), two rebounds, 10 assists, four steals and one block in Wednesday’s win over the Clippers.
 Mitchell’s start to the season has been better than most fantasy managers expected, with the Heat guard providing top-50 per-game value. He couldn’t buy a three-pointer on Wednesday, missing all five attempts, but Mitchell offered excellent production in assists and steals. And even with Wednesday’s poor shooting, Mitchell is still shooting 50 percent from the field this season.

 Bam Adebayo recorded 35 points (14-of-20 FGs, 6-of-8 FTs), 10 rebounds, four assists, one steal and one three-pointer in Wednesday’s win over the Clippers.
 This was a big night for Adebayo, who recorded his first double-double of the season with new highs in points and rebounds. Add in the assists, and it was a good night for those rostering the Heat captain. Even with there still being some bumps the Heat need to smooth over as they work Giannis Antetokounmpo into the fold, Adebayo has been close to a top-25 player in 12-team leagues. That’s encouraging, to say the least.
